rows.question: Analyze the average percentage change in sales between the 12 weeks before and after June 15, 2020, for each attribute type: region, platform, age band, demographic, and customer type. For each attribute type, calculate the average percentage change in sales across all its attribute values. Identify the attribute type with the highest negative impact on sales and provide its average percentage change in sales.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH sales_with_attributes AS (
SELECT
  -- sale_id: construct a stable id per weekly row using week_date + region + platform + segment + customer_type + age_band + demographic
  week_date || '|' || region || '|' || platform || '|' || segment || '|' || customer_type || '|' || COALESCE(age_band,'') || '|' || COALESCE(demographic,'') AS sale_id,
  -- sale_date: use canonical week_date
  week_date AS sale_date,
  -- amount: use sales as the monetary amount for the denormalized sale row
  sales AS amount,
  -- period_label: year-month label composed from calendar_year and month_number
  calendar_year || '-' || printf('%02d', month_number) AS period_label,
  -- attributes: pass through region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type
  region,
  platform,
  age_band,
  demographic,
  customer_type
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
),
sales_pre_post_cohort AS (
SELECT
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY week_date) AS sale_id,
  week_date AS sale_date,
  sales AS amount,
  CASE
    WHEN date(week_date) BETWEEN date(reference_dates.ref_date, '-84 days') AND date(reference_dates.ref_date, '-1 day') THEN 'pre'
    WHEN date(week_date) BETWEEN date(reference_dates.ref_date, '+1 day') AND date(reference_dates.ref_date, '+84 days') THEN 'post'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS period_label
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales,
(
  SELECT
    -- placeholder reference date column; consumers of this view must join or replace this CTE
    NULL AS ref_date
) AS reference_dates
WHERE
  -- keep only rows that fall into either pre or post windows relative to the reference date
  (date(week_date) BETWEEN date(reference_dates.ref_date, '-84 days') AND date(reference_dates.ref_date, '-1 day'))
  OR
  (date(week_date) BETWEEN date(reference_dates.ref_date, '+1 day') AND date(reference_dates.ref_date, '+84 days'))
),
attribute_value_period_totals AS (
SELECT
  attribute_type,
  attribute_value,
  period_label,
  SUM(amount) AS total_sales,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN amount IS NOT NULL AND amount != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_sales_flag
FROM (
  SELECT 'region' AS attribute_type, region AS attribute_value, period_label, amount
  FROM sales_with_attributes
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'platform' AS attribute_type, platform AS attribute_value, period_label, amount
  FROM sales_with_attributes
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'age_band' AS attribute_type, age_band AS attribute_value, period_label, amount
  FROM sales_with_attributes
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'demographic' AS attribute_type, demographic AS attribute_value, period_label, amount
  FROM sales_with_attributes
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'customer_type' AS attribute_type, customer_type AS attribute_value, period_label, amount
  FROM sales_with_attributes
) attrs
GROUP BY attribute_type, attribute_value, period_label
),
attribute_value_percentage_changes AS (
SELECT
  avt.attribute_type AS attribute_type,
  avt.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS pre_sales,
  SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'post' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS post_sales,
  (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'post' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL)
   - CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL))
   / NULLIF(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL), 0) AS percentage_change,
  AVG((CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'post' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL)
       - CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL))
       / NULLIF(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL), 0)
      ) OVER (PARTITION BY avt.attribute_type) AS average_percentage_change_per_attribute_type
FROM attribute_value_period_totals AS avt
GROUP BY
  avt.attribute_type,
  avt.attribute_value
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'post' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END) != 0
  AND (SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'pre' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END)
       + SUM(CASE WHEN avt.period_label = 'post' THEN avt.total_sales ELSE 0 END)) > 0
)
SELECT
  attribute_type,
  average_percentage_change_per_attribute_type AS average_percentage_change,
  (SELECT attribute_type FROM attribute_value_percentage_changes GROUP BY attribute_type ORDER BY AVG(percentage_change) ASC LIMIT 1) AS attribute_type_with_highest_negative_impact,
  (SELECT AVG(percentage_change) FROM attribute_value_percentage_changes GROUP BY attribute_type ORDER BY AVG(percentage_change) ASC LIMIT 1) AS highest_negative_average_percentage_change
FROM (
  SELECT attribute_type, average_percentage_change_per_attribute_type
  FROM attribute_value_percentage_changes
  GROUP BY attribute_type, average_percentage_change_per_attribute_type
) 
ORDER BY attribute_type

rows.question: Considering only the customers who placed orders in 1998, calculate the total amount each customer spent by summing the unit price multiplied by the quantity of all products in their orders, excluding any discounts. WITH orders_1998 AS (

  orderid AS order_id,
  customerid AS customer_id,
  orderdate AS order_date

WHERE orderdate >= '1998-01-01' AND orderdate < '1999-01-01'

  o.customer_id AS customer_id,

spend_group_counts AS (

  cgt.groupname AS spending_group_name,

rows.question: Among employees who have more than 50 total orders, which three have the highest percentage of late orders, where an order is considered late if the shipped date is on or after its required date? Please list each employee's ID, the number of late orders, and the corresponding late-order percentage.

WITH employee_orders AS (
SELECT
  e.employeeid AS employee_id,
  o.orderid AS order_id,
  o.orderdate AS order_date,
  o.requireddate AS required_date,
  o.shippeddate AS shipped_date
FROM orders o
JOIN employees e
  ON o.employeeid = e.employeeid
),
employee_late_rate AS (
SELECT
  e.employeeid AS employee_id,
  COUNT(o.orderid) AS total_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.shippeddate IS NOT NULL AND o.shippeddate > o.requireddate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(o.orderid) = 0 THEN 0.0

  END AS late_percentage
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON e.employeeid = o.employeeid
GROUP BY e.employeeid
),

  o.orderid AS order_id,

FROM orders o
),

The quintile should be determined by calculating how many students have grades greater than or equal to each student's grade, then dividing this ranking by the total number of students who completed English courses. The quintiles should be labeled as "First" (top 20%), "Second" (top 21-40%), "Third" (top 41-60%), "Fourth" (top 61-80%), and "Fifth" (bottom 20%). Please sort the results from highest performing quintile to lowest (First to Fifth).

WITH english_enrollments_completed AS (
  SELECT
    ss.ClassID AS course_id,
    ss.StudentID AS student_id,
    s.StudLastName AS last_name,

  JOIN Subjects subj ON subj.SubjectID = c.SubjectID

      ELSE CAST(grade AS REAL)
    END AS grade

)
SELECT

    WHEN proportion_ge > 0.20 AND proportion_ge <= 0.40 THEN 'Second'
    WHEN proportion_ge > 0.40 AND proportion_ge <= 0.60 THEN 'Third'

rows.question: Given a database of musical styles and user preferences, where Musical_Preferences contains user rankings of musical styles (PreferenceSeq=1 for first choice, PreferenceSeq=2 for second choice, PreferenceSeq=3 for third choice): Calculate a weighted score for each musical style by assigning 3 points for each time it was ranked as first choice, 2 points for each second choice, and 1 point for each third choice ranking. Calculate the total weighted score for each musical style that has been ranked by at least one user. Then, compute the absolute difference between each style's total weighted score and the average total weighted score across all such styles.

  Musical_Preferences.PreferenceSeq AS preference_seq

  AND Musical_Preferences.PreferenceSeq IN (1, 2, 3)

rows.question: Determine the top three genres with the most movies rated above 8, and then identify the top four directors who have directed the most films rated above 8 within those genres. List these directors and their respective movie counts.

  FROM high_rated

),

rows.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE final_packaging_combinations AS (
SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id AS final_combination_id
FROM packaging_relations
),
packaging_edges AS (
SELECT
  packaging_id AS container_id,
  contains_id AS contained_item_id,
  qty AS quantity_per_container
FROM packaging_relations
),
expanded_leaf_quantities AS (
SELECT
  f.final_combination_id,
  e.leaf_item_id,
  e.effective_quantity
FROM (
  WITH RECURSIVE
  -- start from each final combination as a root, seed paths with direct edges
  expansion(root_final_combination_id, path_id, current_item_id, effective_quantity, is_leaf) AS (
    SELECT
      f.final_combination_id AS root_final_combination_id,
      printf('%d', f.final_combination_id) || '-' || printf('%d', pe.contained_item_id) AS path_id,
      pe.contained_item_id AS current_item_id,
      pe.quantity_per_container AS effective_quantity,
      -- determine leafness by existence of outgoing edges from this contained_item_id
      NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM packaging_edges pe2 WHERE pe2.container_id = pe.contained_item_id) AS is_leaf
    FROM final_packaging_combinations f
    JOIN packaging_edges pe ON pe.container_id = f.final_combination_id
    UNION ALL
    -- recurse: expand current_item_id if it is a container (has contained items)
    SELECT
      exp.root_final_combination_id,
      exp.path_id || '-' || printf('%d', pe.contained_item_id) AS path_id,
      pe.contained_item_id AS current_item_id,
      exp.effective_quantity * pe.quantity_per_container AS effective_quantity,
      NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM packaging_edges pe2 WHERE pe2.container_id = pe.contained_item_id) AS is_leaf
    FROM expansion exp
    JOIN packaging_edges pe ON pe.container_id = exp.current_item_id
  )
  -- select only leaf nodes, emit one row per leaf occurrence with effective quantity
  SELECT
    root_final_combination_id AS final_combination_id,
    current_item_id AS leaf_item_id,
    effective_quantity AS effective_quantity
  FROM expansion
  WHERE is_leaf
) e
JOIN final_packaging_combinations f ON f.final_combination_id = e.final_combination_id
),
per_combination_leaf_totals AS (
SELECT
  elq.final_combination_id AS final_combination_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(elq.effective_quantity), 0) AS total_leaf_quantity
FROM
  expanded_leaf_quantities elq
GROUP BY
  elq.final_combination_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_leaf_quantity) AS average_total_quantity
FROM per_combination_leaf_totals

  -- use ROW_NUMBER to produce a deterministic sequence position per product (FIFO rank)

rows.question: Which products were picked for order 421, and what is the average number of units picked for each product, using FIFO (First-In, First-Out) method?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH product_inventory_lots AS (
SELECT
  inventory.id AS inventory_lot_id,
  inventory.product_id AS product_id,
  purchases.purchased AS lot_received_timestamp,
  inventory.qty AS lot_available_quantity
FROM inventory
LEFT JOIN purchases ON purchases.id = inventory.purchase_id
),
order_picks_cohort AS (
SELECT
  picking_log.picklist_id || '-' || picking_log.log_time AS pick_id,
  picking_line.order_id AS order_id,
  picking_line.product_id AS product_id,
  picking_log.log_time AS pick_timestamp,
  -- pick quantity: correlate picking_line.qty as the amount applied by that pick event when pickline matches
  CASE
    WHEN picking_log.pickline_no = picking_line.line_no AND picking_log.picklist_id = picking_line.picklist_id
    THEN picking_line.qty
    ELSE NULL
  END AS picked_quantity,
  -- inventory lot id: there is no direct inventory link in picking_log; leave as NULL unless later joined
  NULL AS inventory_lot_id
FROM picking_log
JOIN picking_line
  ON picking_log.picklist_id = picking_line.picklist_id
  AND picking_log.pickline_no = picking_line.line_no
),
order_product_fifo_picks AS (
SELECT
  pl.order_id AS order_id,
  pl.product_id AS product_id,
  inv.id AS inventory_lot_id,
  pl.picklist_id || '-' || pl.line_no AS pick_id,
  (
    -- quantity allocated to this pick from this inventory lot following FIFO consumption:
    -- it's the minimum of:
    --  1) remaining available qty in the lot at time of consumption
    --  2) pick line quantity (pl.qty) minus quantity already allocated from earlier FIFO lots for same pick
    -- We compute using windowed cumulative sums ordered by inventory.id (proxy for FIFO by purchase order)
    -- and then derive the overlap (allocated portion) between cumulative ranges.
    CASE
      WHEN lot_running_available_before <= 0 THEN 0
      ELSE
        (
          -- overlap between [lot_running_available_before+1, lot_running_available_after] and
          -- [pick_consumed_start, pick_consumed_end]
          (
            (CASE WHEN lot_running_available_after < pick_consumed_start THEN 0
                  WHEN lot_running_available_before+1 > pick_consumed_end THEN 0
                  ELSE
                    (MIN(lot_running_available_after, pick_consumed_end)
                     - MAX(lot_running_available_before+1, pick_consumed_start) + 1)
             END)
          )
        )
    END
  ) * 1.0 AS quantity_allocated_to_order_from_lot
FROM
  picking_line pl
JOIN
  inventory inv ON inv.product_id = pl.product_id
-- compute FIFO ordering per product by inventory.id ascending (as proxy for lot receipt)
-- derive running available before/after for each lot per product
JOIN (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    id AS inventory_lot_id,
    qty AS lot_available_quantity,
    COALESCE(
      SUM(qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING),
      0
    ) AS lot_running_available_before,
    SUM(qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS lot_running_available_after
  FROM inventory
) fifo ON fifo.product_id = inv.product_id AND fifo.inventory_lot_id = inv.id
-- compute for each pick (identified by picklist_id+line_no) the cumulative consumption window in FIFO coordinate space:
-- pick_consumed_start..pick_consumed_end are 1-based positions into the product's total FIFO sequence
JOIN (
  SELECT
    pl2.picklist_id || '-' || pl2.line_no AS pick_id,
    pl2.order_id,
    pl2.product_id,
    pl2.qty AS pick_qty,
    -- pick_consumed_end: cumulative sum of picks for this product up to and including this pick
    COALESCE(
      SUM(pl2.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY pl2.product_id ORDER BY pl2.picklist_id, pl2.line_no ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),
      0
    ) AS pick_consumed_end,
    -- pick_consumed_start is end minus this pick qty plus 1 (1-based)
    (COALESCE(
      SUM(pl2.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY pl2.product_id ORDER BY pl2.picklist_id, pl2.line_no ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),
      0
    ) - pl2.qty + 1) AS pick_consumed_start
  FROM picking_line pl2
) pc ON pc.order_id = pl.order_id AND pc.product_id = pl.product_id AND pc.pick_id = pl.picklist_id || '-' || pl.line_no
),
fifo_allocations_per_lot AS (
SELECT
  pil.inventory_lot_id AS product_id,
  pil.inventory_lot_id,
  pil.lot_received_timestamp,
  pil.lot_available_quantity,
  -- running available before this lot = sum of available_qty of all older lots for same product
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(pil2.lot_available_quantity)
    FROM product_inventory_lots pil2
    WHERE pil2.product_id = pil.product_id
      AND (
        pil2.lot_received_timestamp < pil.lot_received_timestamp
        OR (pil2.lot_received_timestamp = pil.lot_received_timestamp AND pil2.inventory_lot_id < pil.inventory_lot_id)
      )
  ), 0) AS lot_running_available_before,
  -- running available after = before + this lot's available
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(pil2.lot_available_quantity)
    FROM product_inventory_lots pil2
    WHERE pil2.product_id = pil.product_id
      AND (
        pil2.lot_received_timestamp < pil.lot_received_timestamp
        OR (pil2.lot_received_timestamp = pil.lot_received_timestamp AND pil2.inventory_lot_id <= pil.inventory_lot_id)
      )
  ), 0) AS lot_running_available_after,
  -- fifo rank: 1 = oldest; tie-breaker by inventory_lot_id
  (
    SELECT COUNT(1)
    FROM product_inventory_lots pil3
    WHERE pil3.product_id = pil.product_id
      AND (
        pil3.lot_received_timestamp < pil.lot_received_timestamp
        OR (pil3.lot_received_timestamp = pil.lot_received_timestamp AND pil3.inventory_lot_id <= pil.inventory_lot_id)
      )
  ) AS lot_fifo_rank
FROM product_inventory_lots pil
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  AVG(quantity_allocated_to_order_from_lot) AS average_units_picked_per_product
FROM order_product_fifo_picks
WHERE order_id = 421
GROUP BY product_id

rows.question: Based on monthly sales data starting in January 2016 and using a centered moving average to adjust for seasonality, which products had a seasonality-adjusted sales ratio that stayed consistently above 2 for every month in the year 2017?

WITH monthly_sales_cma AS (
  SELECT
    m.product_id AS product_id,
    substr(m.mth,1,7) AS year_month,
    (
      (
        SELECT AVG(ms0.qty)
        FROM monthly_sales ms0
        WHERE ms0.product_id = m.product_id
          AND substr(ms0.mth,1,7) BETWEEN substr(date(m.mth, '-11 months'),1,7) AND substr(m.mth,1,7)
      )
      +
      (
        SELECT AVG(ms1.qty)
        FROM monthly_sales ms1
        WHERE ms1.product_id = m.product_id
          AND substr(ms1.mth,1,7) BETWEEN substr(date(m.mth, '-12 months'),1,7) AND substr(date(m.mth, '-1 month'),1,7)
      )
    ) / 2.0 AS cma_12m
  FROM monthly_sales m
  WHERE m.mth >= '2016-01-01'
),
monthly_sales_raw AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    substr(mth,1,7) AS year_month,
    qty AS sales_amount
  FROM monthly_sales
  WHERE mth >= '2016-01-01'
),
monthly_sales_ratios AS (
  SELECT

    r.year_month,
    r.sales_amount,
    c.cma_12m,
    CASE WHEN c.cma_12m IS NULL OR c.cma_12m = 0 THEN NULL ELSE CAST(r.sales_amount AS REAL) / c.cma_12m END AS sales_to_cma_ratio
  FROM monthly_sales_raw r
  JOIN monthly_sales_cma c
    ON r.product_id = c.product_id
   AND r.year_month = c.year_month
),

rows.question: Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December 2018 inventory levels, where we restock a product if its ending inventory drops below the minimum required level, determine for each product the month in 2019 where the absolute difference between its ending inventory and the minimum required level is the smallest, and return the product_id, that month, and the absolute difference.

WITH RECURSIVE monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS (
SELECT
  p.id AS product_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m', m.mth) AS year_month,
  COALESCE(r.receipts, 0) AS receipts,
  COALESCE(s.shipments, 0) AS shipments
FROM products p
-- build 2019 months (intrinsic filter: 2019-01 through 2019-12)
JOIN (
  SELECT date('2019-01-01', ('+' || (n) || ' months')) AS mth
  FROM (
    SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL
    SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL
    SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
  )
) m ON 1=1
LEFT JOIN (
  -- receipts per product-month: sum of purchases.qty where purchased in that month
  SELECT
    product_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', purchased) AS year_month,
    SUM(qty) AS receipts
  FROM purchases
  GROUP BY product_id, strftime('%Y-%m', purchased)
) r ON r.product_id = p.id AND r.year_month = strftime('%Y-%m', m.mth)
LEFT JOIN (
  -- shipments per product-month: sum of orderlines.qty where orders.ordered in that month
  SELECT
    ol.product_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', o.ordered) AS year_month,
    SUM(ol.qty) AS shipments
  FROM orderlines ol
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = ol.order_id
  GROUP BY ol.product_id, strftime('%Y-%m', o.ordered)
) s ON s.product_id = p.id AND s.year_month = strftime('%Y-%m', m.mth)
),
initial_december_end_inventory AS (
SELECT
  p.id AS product_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(i.qty), 0.0) AS dec_2018_ending_inventory
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN inventory i
  ON i.product_id = p.id
  AND i.purchase_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM purchases WHERE purchased <= '2018-12-29'
  )
GROUP BY p.id
),
product_minimum_levels AS (
SELECT
  pm.product_id AS product_id,
  COALESCE(pm.qty_minimum, 0.0) AS minimum_required_level
FROM product_minimums pm
),
monthly_inventory_recursive_2019 AS (
SELECT
  p.id AS product_id,
  -- year_month in format 'YYYY-MM-01' for each month of 2019 will be derived by caller; here expose month identifiers by joining receipts/shipments and allowing months to be supplied.
  m.year_month AS year_month,
  -- beginning_inventory: prior month's ending inventory. We compute iterative by starting from initial_december_end_inventory and adding cumulative receipts - shipments up to prior month.
  COALESCE(
    idei.dec_2018_ending_inventory
    + IFNULL((
        SELECT SUM(r.receipts - r.shipments)
        FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS r
        WHERE r.product_id = p.id
          AND r.year_month < m.year_month
      ), 0.0),
    0.0
  ) AS beginning_inventory,
  -- raw ending before applying minimum: beginning + receipts - shipments for this month
  (
    COALESCE(
      idei.dec_2018_ending_inventory
      + IFNULL((
          SELECT SUM(r.receipts - r.shipments)
          FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS r
          WHERE r.product_id = p.id
            AND r.year_month < m.year_month
        ), 0.0),
      0.0
    )
    + IFNULL(mrs.receipts, 0.0)
    - IFNULL(mrs.shipments, 0.0)
  ) AS raw_ending_inventory,
  -- minimum_required_level from product_minimum_levels view
  COALESCE(pml.minimum_required_level, 0.0) AS minimum_required_level,
  -- ending_inventory after enforcing minimum
  CASE
    WHEN (
      COALESCE(
        idei.dec_2018_ending_inventory
        + IFNULL((
            SELECT SUM(r.receipts - r.shipments)
            FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS r
            WHERE r.product_id = p.id
              AND r.year_month < m.year_month
          ), 0.0),
        0.0
      )
      + IFNULL(mrs.receipts, 0.0)
      - IFNULL(mrs.shipments, 0.0)
    ) < COALESCE(pml.minimum_required_level, 0.0)
    THEN COALESCE(pml.minimum_required_level, 0.0)
    ELSE (
      COALESCE(
        idei.dec_2018_ending_inventory
        + IFNULL((
            SELECT SUM(r.receipts - r.shipments)
            FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS r
            WHERE r.product_id = p.id
              AND r.year_month < m.year_month
          ), 0.0),
        0.0
      )
      + IFNULL(mrs.receipts, 0.0)
      - IFNULL(mrs.shipments, 0.0)
    )
  END AS ending_inventory,
  -- abs_diff between ending_inventory and minimum_required_level
  ABS(
    CASE
      WHEN (
        COALESCE(
          idei.dec_2018_ending_inventory
          + IFNULL((
              SELECT SUM(r.receipts - r.shipments)
              FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS r
              WHERE r.product_id = p.id
                AND r.year_month < m.year_month
            ), 0.0),
          0.0
        )
        + IFNULL(mrs.receipts, 0.0)
        - IFNULL(mrs.shipments, 0.0)
      ) < COALESCE(pml.minimum_required_level, 0.0)
      THEN COALESCE(pml.minimum_required_level, 0.0)
      ELSE (
        COALESCE(
          idei.dec_2018_ending_inventory
          + IFNULL((
              SELECT SUM(r.receipts - r.shipments)
              FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS r
              WHERE r.product_id = p.id
                AND r.year_month < m.year_month
            ), 0.0),
          0.0
        )
        + IFNULL(mrs.receipts, 0.0)
        - IFNULL(mrs.shipments, 0.0)
      )
    END
    - COALESCE(pml.minimum_required_level, 0.0)
  ) AS abs_diff
FROM products AS p
-- ensure every product-month for 2019 is available by selecting distinct year_months from monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT year_month FROM monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019
) AS m ON 1=1
LEFT JOIN monthly_receipts_and_shipments_2019 AS mrs
  ON mrs.product_id = p.id AND mrs.year_month = m.year_month
LEFT JOIN product_minimum_levels AS pml
  ON pml.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN initial_december_end_inventory AS idei
  ON idei.product_id = p.id
)
SELECT
  m.product_id,
  MIN(m.year_month) AS month,
  MIN(m.abs_diff) AS abs_diff
FROM monthly_inventory_recursive_2019 m
GROUP BY m.product_id
ORDER BY m.product_id

seller_category_sales AS (
SELECT
  oi.seller_id AS seller_id,
  p.product_category_name AS category_id,
  pct.product_category_name_english AS category_name_en,
  SUM(1) AS category_quantity_sold,
  SUM(oi.price) AS category_sales_amount
FROM
  order_items oi
JOIN
  products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN
  product_category_name_translation pct
  ON p.product_category_name = pct.product_category_name
GROUP BY
  oi.seller_id,
  p.product_category_name
),
seller_item_level_metrics AS (
SELECT
  se.seller_id AS seller_id,
  se.product_id AS product_id,
  se.category_id AS category_id,
  se.category_name_en AS category_name_en,
  se.order_id AS order_id,
  -- ensure quantity is numeric and default to 1 when missing or non-positive
  CASE
    WHEN se.quantity IS NULL THEN 1.0
    WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 1.0
    WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) <= 0 THEN 1.0
    ELSE CAST(se.quantity AS REAL)
  END AS quantity,
  -- ensure unit_price is numeric and non-negative, default 0.0
  CASE
    WHEN se.unit_price IS NULL THEN 0.0
    WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 0.0
    WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) < 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL)
  END AS unit_price,
  -- ensure line_revenue is numeric; if missing compute quantity * unit_price, else coerce and fallback to computed
  CASE
    WHEN se.line_revenue IS NULL THEN
      (CASE
        WHEN (CASE WHEN se.quantity IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) <= 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) END) IS NULL THEN 0.0
        WHEN (CASE WHEN se.unit_price IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) END) IS NULL THEN 0.0
        ELSE (CASE WHEN se.quantity IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) <= 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) END) * (CASE WHEN se.unit_price IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) END)
      END)
    WHEN CAST(se.line_revenue AS REAL) IS NULL THEN
      (CASE
        WHEN (CASE WHEN se.quantity IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) <= 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) END) IS NULL THEN 0.0
        WHEN (CASE WHEN se.unit_price IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) END) IS NULL THEN 0.0
        ELSE (CASE WHEN se.quantity IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 1.0 WHEN CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) <= 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE CAST(se.quantity AS REAL) END) * (CASE WHEN se.unit_price IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) IS NULL THEN 0.0 WHEN CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE CAST(se.unit_price AS REAL) END)
      END)
    WHEN CAST(se.line_revenue AS REAL) < 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE CAST(se.line_revenue AS REAL)
  END AS line_revenue,
  -- normalize review_score to integer between 1 and 5, NULL if not present or out of range
  CASE
    WHEN se.review_score IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(se.review_score AS INTEGER) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(se.review_score AS INTEGER) < 1 OR CAST(se.review_score AS INTEGER) > 5 THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(se.review_score AS INTEGER)
  END AS review_score,
  -- packing_time: ensure numeric non-negative, NULL when missing or invalid
  CASE
    WHEN se.packing_time IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(se.packing_time AS REAL) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(se.packing_time AS REAL) < 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(se.packing_time AS REAL)
  END AS packing_time
FROM seller_sales_events se
),
seller_performance_summary AS (
SELECT
  sss.seller_id AS seller_id,
  sss.seller_name AS seller_name,
  SUM(sss.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold,
  SUM(sss.line_revenue) AS total_sales,
  CASE WHEN SUM(sss.quantity) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(sss.line_revenue) * 1.0 / SUM(sss.quantity) END AS avg_item_price,
  AVG(sss.review_score) AS avg_review_score,
  AVG(sss.packing_time) AS avg_packing_time,
  scs_top.category_name_en AS top_category_name_en,
  scs_top.category_quantity_sold AS top_category_quantity_sold
FROM
  seller_sales_events sss
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    category_name_en,
    category_quantity_sold,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_id ORDER BY category_quantity_sold DESC) AS rn
  FROM seller_category_sales
) scs_top ON sss.seller_id = scs_top.seller_id AND scs_top.rn = 1
GROUP BY
  sss.seller_id,
  sss.seller_name,
  scs_top.category_name_en,
  scs_top.category_quantity_sold
HAVING
  SUM(sss.quantity) > 100
)
SELECT
  seller_id,
  seller_name,
  total_sales,
  avg_item_price,
  avg_review_score,
  avg_packing_time,
  top_category_name_en,
  top_category_quantity_sold
FROM seller_performance_summary
WHERE total_quantity_sold > 100
ORDER BY total_sales DESC

rows.question: How many unique sessions visited the /regist/input page and then the /regist/confirm page, in that order?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH session_events_filtered AS (
SELECT
  session AS session_id,
  stamp AS event_timestamp,
  path AS page_path,
  rowid AS event_row_id
FROM form_log
WHERE path IN ('/regist/input', '/regist/confirm')
),
sessions_input_before_confirm AS (
SELECT
  fh.session AS session_id
FROM (
  SELECT
    session,
    MIN(stamp) AS first_input_ts
  FROM form_log
  WHERE path = '/input'
  GROUP BY session
) fh
JOIN (
  SELECT
    session,
    MIN(stamp) AS first_confirm_ts
  FROM form_log
  WHERE path = '/confirm'
  GROUP BY session
) fc
  ON fh.session = fc.session
WHERE fh.first_input_ts < fc.first_confirm_ts
),
session_event_ordered AS (
SELECT
  session_id,
  event_timestamp,
  page_path,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) AS event_rank_in_session
FROM session_events_filtered
),
session_has_input_and_confirm_flags AS (
SELECT
  se.session_id AS session_id,
  CASE WHEN MIN(CASE WHEN se.page_path = '/regist/input' THEN se.event_timestamp END) IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS exists_input,
  CASE WHEN MIN(CASE WHEN se.page_path = '/regist/confirm' THEN se.event_timestamp END) IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS exists_confirm,
  MIN(CASE WHEN se.page_path = '/regist/input' THEN se.event_timestamp END) AS first_input_ts,
  MIN(CASE WHEN se.page_path = '/regist/confirm' THEN se.event_timestamp END) AS first_confirm_ts
FROM session_event_ordered se
WHERE se.page_path IN ('/regist/input','/regist/confirm')
GROUP BY se.session_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS count
FROM sessions_input_before_confirm

rows.question: Using the activity log table, compute the total number of unique user sessions where each web page appears as either a landing page (the first page visited in a session based on timestamp) or an exit page (the last page visited in a session based on timestamp), or both. Count each session only once per page even if the page serves as both landing and exit for that session.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH session_events_filtered AS (
SELECT
  session AS session_id,
  stamp AS event_timestamp,
  path AS page_path,
  rowid AS event_row_id
FROM form_log
WHERE path IN ('/regist/input', '/regist/confirm')
),
activity_rows_with_sessions AS (
SELECT
  session AS session_id,
  stamp AS timestamp,
  path AS page
FROM activity_log
WHERE session IS NOT NULL
  AND session <> ''
),
session_landing_and_exit_rows AS (
SELECT
  se.session_id AS session_id,
  se.page_path AS landing_page,
  ex.page_path AS exit_page
FROM
  -- landing rows: rows that have the minimum event_timestamp per session
  session_events_filtered se
JOIN
  (
    SELECT session_id, MIN(event_timestamp) AS min_ts
    FROM session_events_filtered
    GROUP BY session_id
  ) min_ts_per_s
  ON se.session_id = min_ts_per_s.session_id
  AND se.event_timestamp = min_ts_per_s.min_ts
JOIN
  -- exit rows: choose one of the rows having the maximum event_timestamp per session
  (
    SELECT session_id, page_path, event_timestamp
    FROM session_events_filtered
  ) ex
  ON ex.session_id = se.session_id
  AND ex.event_timestamp = (
    SELECT MAX(event_timestamp) FROM session_events_filtered WHERE session_id = se.session_id
  )
),
page_session_counts AS (
SELECT
  p.page AS page,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.session_id) AS session_count
FROM (
  SELECT session_id, landing_page AS page FROM session_landing_and_exit_rows WHERE landing_page IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT session_id, exit_page AS page FROM session_landing_and_exit_rows WHERE exit_page IS NOT NULL
) p
GROUP BY p.page
),
session_page_pairs AS (
SELECT
  session_id,
  landing_page AS page
FROM session_landing_and_exit_rows
UNION
SELECT
  session_id,
  exit_page AS page
FROM session_landing_and_exit_rows
)
SELECT page, session_count
FROM page_session_counts
ORDER BY session_count DESC

rows.question: Which three distinct third-page visits are most frequently observed immediately after two consecutive visits to the '/detail' page, and how many times does each third-page visit occur?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ordered_user_sequences AS (
SELECT
  al.user_id AS user_id,
  al.session AS session_id,
  al.stamp AS event_timestamp,
  al.category AS page_1,
  LEAD(al.category, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY al.session ORDER BY al.stamp, rowid) AS page_2,
  LEAD(al.category, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY al.session ORDER BY al.stamp, rowid) AS page_3,
  rowid AS event_id
FROM action_log al
),
detail_detail_third_candidates AS (
SELECT
  ordered_user_sequences.user_id AS user_id,
  ordered_user_sequences.session_id AS session_id,
  ordered_user_sequences.event_timestamp AS event_timestamp,
  ordered_user_sequences.page_3 AS third_page
FROM ordered_user_sequences
WHERE ordered_user_sequences.page_1 = '/detail'
  AND ordered_user_sequences.page_2 = '/detail'
  AND ordered_user_sequences.page_1 IS NOT NULL
  AND ordered_user_sequences.page_2 IS NOT NULL
  AND ordered_user_sequences.page_3 IS NOT NULL
),
third_page_counts AS (
SELECT
  third_page AS third_page,
  COUNT(*) AS count
FROM
  detail_detail_third_candidates
GROUP BY
  third_page
)
SELECT
  third_page,
  COUNT(*) AS count
FROM detail_detail_third_candidates
GROUP BY third_page
ORDER BY count DESC
LIMIT 3

rows.question: How many users are there in each age category (20s, 30s, 40s, 50s, and others)?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH users_raw AS (
SELECT
  user_id,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(birth_date) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (strftime('%Y', 'now') - strftime('%Y', birth_date)) - 
      (strftime('%m-%d', 'now') < strftime('%m-%d', birth_date))
  END AS age
FROM mst_users
),
users_age_normalized AS (
SELECT
  user_id,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(age) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN age IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(age AS INTEGER) IS NOT NULL AND age LIKE '%[^0-9]%' = 0 AND instr(age, '.') = 0 THEN CAST(age AS INTEGER)
    WHEN age GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN CAST(age AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      (CASE
         WHEN age GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN
           -- extract leading integer digits
           CAST(substr(age, 1,
             (CASE
                WHEN instr(age, ' ')>0 THEN instr(age,' ')-1
                WHEN instr(age,'-')>0 THEN instr(age,'-')-1
                WHEN instr(age,'/')>0 THEN instr(age,'/')-1
                ELSE
                  (SELECT
                     CASE
                       WHEN instr(age, '.')>0 THEN instr(age,'.')-1
                       WHEN instr(age, ',')>0 THEN instr(age,',')-1
                       ELSE length(age)
                     END
                   )
              END
             )
           ) AS INTEGER)
         ELSE NULL
       END)
  END AS age_clean
FROM users_raw
),
users_with_age_category AS (
SELECT
  u.user_id,
  CASE
    WHEN a.age_clean BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN '20s'
    WHEN a.age_clean BETWEEN 30 AND 39 THEN '30s'
    WHEN a.age_clean BETWEEN 40 AND 49 THEN '40s'
    WHEN a.age_clean BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN '50s'
    ELSE 'others'
  END AS age_category
FROM users_age_normalized a
JOIN mst_users u USING (user_id)
),
user_count_per_age_category AS (
SELECT
  coalesce(uac.age_category, 'unknown') AS age_category,
  COUNT(m.user_id) AS user_count
FROM mst_users m
LEFT JOIN users_with_age_category uac
  ON m.user_id = uac.user_id
GROUP BY coalesce(uac.age_category, 'unknown')
)
SELECT age_category, user_count
FROM user_count_per_age_category
ORDER BY CASE age_category
  WHEN '20s' THEN 1
  WHEN '30s' THEN 2
  WHEN '40s' THEN 3
  WHEN '50s' THEN 4
  WHEN 'others' THEN 5
  ELSE 6 END

rows.question: For each user session in the activity log table, identify the number of events that occurred before the first '/detail' click or '/complete' conversion, counting only events that have a non-empty search type. Find the sessions with the minimum count of such pre-click/pre-conversion events. If multiple sessions share this minimum count, include all of them in the results. Return each qualifying session along with the corresponding path and search type.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH pre_click_counts_and_min_sessions AS (
SELECT
  al.session AS session,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE al.search_type IS NOT NULL AND al.search_type <> '') AS pre_click_pre_conversion_count,
  al.path AS path,
  al.search_type AS search_type
FROM activity_log al
WHERE al.search_type IS NOT NULL AND al.search_type <> ''
GROUP BY al.session, al.path, al.search_type
HAVING COUNT(*) = (
  SELECT MIN(sess_count) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS sess_count
    FROM activity_log al2
    WHERE al2.search_type IS NOT NULL AND al2.search_type <> ''
    GROUP BY al2.session
  )
)
),
session_events_raw AS (
SELECT
  session AS session,
  rowid AS event_id,
  stamp AS event_timestamp,
  path AS path,
  search_type AS search_type,
  NULL AS event_order
FROM activity_log
WHERE session IN (
  SELECT DISTINCT session FROM activity_log WHERE path = '/detail' OR path = '/complete'
)
),
session_first_detail_or_complete AS (
SELECT
  session AS session,
  MIN(rowid) AS first_dc_event_id,
  MIN(stamp) AS first_dc_event_timestamp,
  MIN(rowid) AS first_dc_event_order
FROM (
  SELECT rowid, stamp, session, path FROM activity_log
  UNION ALL
  SELECT rowid, stamp, session, path FROM form_log
)
WHERE path IN ('/detail', '/complete')
GROUP BY session
)
SELECT ser.session,
       ser.path,
       ser.search_type,
       pc.pre_click_pre_conversion_count
FROM session_first_detail_or_complete fdc
JOIN (
    SELECT session, COUNT(*) AS pre_click_pre_conversion_count
    FROM session_events_raw
    WHERE search_type IS NOT NULL
      AND search_type <> ''
    GROUP BY session
) pc ON pc.session = fdc.session
JOIN session_events_raw ser
  ON ser.session = fdc.session
 AND ser.event_order < fdc.first_dc_event_order
 AND ser.search_type IS NOT NULL
 AND ser.search_type <> ''
WHERE pc.pre_click_pre_conversion_count = (
    SELECT MIN(pre_click_pre_conversion_count)
    FROM (
      SELECT session, COUNT(*) AS pre_click_pre_conversion_count
      FROM session_events_raw
      WHERE search_type IS NOT NULL
        AND search_type <> ''
      GROUP BY session
    )
)
